reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the premise that increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides enhances CO oxidation activity and durability, but it does not address fluorite oxides, Pd single-atom dispersion, or the specific performance metrics claimed for the Pd/HEFO system. Key premises about the support material, active metal, and predicted outcomes are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: High configurational disorder in a metal oxide support improves CO oxidation activity and durability.
A molecular precursor synthesis method can produce a high-entropy oxide with homogeneous elemental distribution.
Atomically dispersing Pd on a high-entropy fluorite oxide will generate abundant oxygen vacancies and strong metal-support interactions.
The proposed Pd/HEFO catalyst will lower CO oxidation onset temperature by ~40% vs. Pd/CeO2 and maintain >95% activity over 14 h.
The Mars–van Krevelen mechanism involving lattice oxygen will be facilitated by the single-atom Pd/HEFO system.
